title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Ops & Top Support Issues
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose

Provide a single, maintained reference for how we produce, review, publish, and operate Developer Experience documentation (SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures), and a canonical list of top support issues with established fixes. This page is intended for DevEx engineers, technical writers, and on-call support engineers who maintain the docs site and customer-facing examples.

Scope

- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go): style, testing, and example coverage expectations
- Quickstarts & templates: repo layout, runnable examples, and license headers
- API examples: canonical request/response snippets, error handling, and streaming patterns
- Docs site operations: publishing workflow, CI checks, rollback steps, and monitoring
- Top support issues & canonical fixes: canonical fixes and diagnostic commands kept in the knowledge base

Roles & Ownership

- Owner: eng-developer-experience (primary contact: Asha Patel)
- Reviewers: Marco Reyes (SDK team), Liang Zhou (Runtime), Priya Nair (Support)
- Docs site infra: eng-platform owns the CI/CD pipeline that publishes the site
- On-call support: eng-sre for infra issues; devex on-call for content triage

Documentation Standards (must-haves for any DevEx doc)

1. Clear title and short description (1-2 sentences).
2. Audience and prerequisites section.
3. Step-by-step quickstarts that are runnable in < 10 minutes.
4. At least one language SDK example (Python + TypeScript preferred).
5. Example inputs/outputs and a minimal test harness.
6. License header and code-of-conduct link for templates.
7. Metadata: owner_team, reviewers, created_at, last_updated, labels.

Templates and Example Table

| Template | Purpose | Required Files | Minimum Reviewers | CI Checks |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| quickstart-template | Bootstrappable app that shows auth + simple call | README.md, example.<lang>, Dockerfile, test.sh | 1 SDK + 1 Support | lint, unit-test, run-example |
| sdk-guide-template | API surface + idiomatic patterns | README.md, usage.md, examples/ | 2 SDK reviewers | lint, compile(/typecheck), example-run |
| api-example-snippet | Single-file request/response examples | snippet.<ext>, README.md | 1 Reviewer | snippet-exec (smoke) |

(Above table is a reference; actual template repos are under github.com/redwood-inference/devex-templates)

Publishing Workflow (Docs Site)

1. Create PR against docs repo branch (docs are Markdown/Confluence-export-ready in our monorepo). Include: short summary, test commands, and checklist.
2. Automated checks run in CI: markdown-lint, link-check, snippet-exec (runs code snippets in containers), spellcheck.
3. At least one reviewer from "devex" team approves. For API changes that affect customers, add a product or support reviewer.
4. Merge triggers site build; build artifacts are published to the staging site at https://staging-docs.redwood.example.com within ~10 minutes.
5. Smoke test: run the smoke checklist (see section below). If smoke fails, revert the build and open urgent PR.
6. After 24 hours on staging and sign-off by owner, promote to production. For urgent security or legal fixes, owners may fast-track to production with <2 reviewers but must retroactively document the reason.

Smoke Checklist (to run after staging build)

- Open top-level quickstart and run full example in container: scripts/run-quickstart.sh
- Validate all external links return 200 (link-check output)
- Verify sample API examples produce expected status codes (200 or expected error)
- Confirm code snippets execute without network credentials where applicable (use mocks)

Docs CI & Snippet Execution (how snippet-exec works)

- snippet-exec containers run code with short timeouts and mocked endpoints for sensitive calls.
- Secrets: CI injects MOCK_ keys for short-lived local mock server; never use real keys in CI.
- Logs: snippet-exec publishes condensed logs to the PR checks; full logs available to devex owners.

Rollback Procedure (site-level incident)

1. Identify bad build: in CI dashboard, mark last-known-good build ID.
2. Use eng-platform runbook: `scripts/docs/rollback.sh --to-build <build-id>` to restore the previous artifact.
3. Notify #docs-alerts, open incident with summary, and assign an owner within 30 minutes.
4. If rollback is not possible, redirect production to staging-hosted content and apply hotfix PR.

SDK Quickstart Example (Python)

Prereqs: python 3.10+, venv, MOCK_API_KEY set for local mock server

# Quickstart: minimal text generation
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${MOCK_API_KEY}")
resp = client.text.generate(model="rw-large-v1", input="Translate to French: Hello")
print(resp.text)
```

CLI / Curl example (canonical API snippet)

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/text/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOCK_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"Summarize: Redwood Inference"}'

Expected response (trimmed):
{
  "id": "resp_12345",
  "model": "rw-large-v1",
  "output": "Redwood Inference is a platform for running and optimizing LLM inference..."
}

API Example Patterns to Document

- idempotent retry semantics and recommended backoff (exponential + jitter)
- streaming examples (client-side processing of partial output)
- function/tool calling pattern (structured JSON outputs + schema validation)
- embeddings best practices: batching sizes, and cosine similarity examples

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (maintain this list in the KB and reference from product release notes)

1. Authentication 401 when users rotate keys
   - Cause: stale key cached in local config or CI secrets
   - Fix: `redwood config set --api-key <new-key>` OR update CI secret and restart pipeline. Add note to quickstart about token caches.

2. Snippets fail in CI due to network timeouts
   - Cause: flaky mock server or missing MOCK_ env vars
   - Fix: re-run snippet-exec after ensuring MOCK_SERVER_URL and MOCK_API_KEY are set; add a short retry in snippet-exec harness.

3. Streaming responses truncated in examples
   - Cause: incorrect use of streaming client (not draining iterator) or example using sync client for async API.
   - Fix: replace with canonical streaming loop (example provided in SDK guides).

4. Version skew: docs show model names that no longer exist
   - Cause: model deprecation not reflected in docs
   - Fix: add a model-version-check job in CI that warns if model in examples is not in the model-catalog API. Create PR to update examples.

5. Missing or broken links after page moves
   - Cause: internal page IDs changed or renames without redirects
   - Fix: use `scripts/docs/link-fix.sh` to scan broken links and add redirects or update references. Add link-check to PRs.

Documentation SLOs (internal)

- Triage SLA for doc-related support tickets: 4 business hours.
- Minor doc update turnaround (typo, 1-2 line change): 2 business days to publication.
- Major doc update (semantic API change): 5 business days with product/support review.
- Critical fixes (security/legal): 6 hours to published hotfix with post-facto review.

Monitoring & Metrics

- Page views and time-on-page for quickstarts (tracked in console) - owners should review weekly.
- CI snippet-exec failure rate - target < 2% of PRs.
- Broken link rate on staging - target 0%.

Operational Playbook for on-call devex engineer

1. Receive alert from #docs-alerts or monitoring (page build failed, broken link spike).
2. Triage: check CI logs, snippet-exec, and staging site.
3. If content-related, create a content-PR and assign reviewer; if infra-related, escalate to eng-platform and run rollback.
4. Communicate status in channel and include estimated time to remediate.

Maintenance Tasks (quarterly)

- Review top 20 quickstart pages for bitrot and update code to match current SDKs.
- Run link-check across full site and fix redirects.
- Re-run snippet-exec with latest mock-server image and address any failures.
- Audit labels and metadata for orphaned pages.

References and Links

- DevEx templates repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-templates
- Docs CI runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/docs-ci-runbook
- Model catalog API: /confluence/product-docs/model-catalog

Appendix: Example PR Checklist (to include in all PR descriptions)

- [ ] Title and short description included
- [ ] Audience and prerequisites documented
- [ ] At least one runnable code example included and verified locally
- [ ] CI checks pass (lint, snippet-exec, link-check)
- [ ] Reviewers assigned and approvals obtained
- [ ] If API change, cross-team reviewer from product/support assigned

Contact

For questions about this playbook, contact Asha Patel (owner) or ping #devex.
